scenes.big: Dust in your eye on the bike?
scenes.say: Got dust in your eye on your bike? Don't rub it. Do this instead.

scenes.en: Rubbing drags grit across the cornea and can scratch it.
scenes.say: The front of your eye, the cornea, is clear and delicate. Rubbing drags the grit across it, and can scratch it.

scenes.en: Pull over safely. Blink. Rinse with clean water.
scenes.say: Pull over safely first. Blink a few times, and rinse with clean water. Tears often wash it out.

scenes.en: Helmet with a clear visor down, or wraparound glasses
scenes.say: Protect your eyes on every ride. Keep a clear helmet visor down, or wear wraparound glasses.

scenes.en: Wind dries your eyes fast, so they water and sting.
scenes.say: Did you know? Strong wind dries your eyes quickly. That's why they water and sting on long rides.

scenes.en: Don't dig it out with a finger, cloth corner or anything sharp.
scenes.say: Don't try to dig it out with your finger, the corner of a cloth, or anything sharp.

scenes.en: Pain, blur, or it still feels stuck after rinsing
scenes.ta: கழுவிய பின்னும் வலி இருந்தால் உடனே மருத்துவரிடம்
scenes.say: See an eye specialist urgently if there's pain, blurred vision, or it still feels stuck after rinsing. Anything that hits your eye at speed is urgent.
Clear vision keeps you safe on the road. Book an eye test today.
